triage.reason: Launch announcement — skim for the three design decisions; the introduction document covers usage better.

digest.summary: Announcement that Second Brain is open source under MIT. Positions the product against read-it-later apps: triage before reading, digest separated from critique, connections across the library. Highlights three decisions: no separate model subscription, plain local files, and an agent that works directly in the user's workspace.

highlights.text: Saving was never the hard part.
Analysis runs through the coding agent you already use — so there is no separate model API key to buy.
The roadmap is negotiable, but the philosophy isn't.

concepts.definition: The filesystem is the single source of truth; the web UI is just a view over the user's own files.

hiddenAssumptions: Readers already have a Claude Code or Codex CLI subscription to reuse.
potentialIssues: Announcement tone: claims about triage quality are not benchmarked here.
needsVerification: Whether extension capture works on the sites you actually read.
biasIndicators: First-party announcement of the product it describes.

connections.summary: The announcement's claims are demonstrated hands-on in the introduction.
connections.details: This piece states the positioning; the Welcome document walks through the loop those claims describe.
